newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end slightly higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end slightly higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Thursday in very quiet trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.05 pct to 102.82
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 101.72.
Volume was a moderate 153 million shekels with most activity concentrated in unlinked bonds.
"The market was very quiet today. Everybody is interested in the stock market and bonds are less attractive now," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.

"CPI-linked bonds closed almost unchanged in very quiet trade. Inflation-linked bonds rose very fast (recently) with yields falling to nearly four percent and now they have to rest," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"Most of the activity was concentrated in unlinked bonds and volume rose to 63 million shekels. Despite that, unlinked bonds posted only mild gains," The FIBI dealer said.

"Makams and unlinked bonds are still attractive for investors who believe that the 1997 inflation will be as low as 8.5 percent. In such a case they still offer yields of five percent," said Michael Politzer, head of the economics department at the Central Securities Corp.
Dollar-linked bonds were today's main gainers and traders said they rose as investors expect that the shekel will continue to decline against the U.S. currency.
On Thursday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3210 shekels against 3.3220 shekels on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
